rationales: kg m s⁻¹ is a unit of momentum, not gravitational field strength.
kg m² s⁻¹ is not the unit of gravitational field strength.
N m² is not the unit of gravitational field strength.
Gravitational field strength is force per unit mass, so its unit is N kg⁻¹.
In a one-dimensional elastic collision, the first particle stops, so its velocity is not v.
The first particle does not reverse direction in a one-dimensional elastic collision with an equal mass initially at rest.
For a one-dimensional elastic collision between equal masses, the moving particle transfers its velocity to the stationary one and stops.
−1/2 is not a velocity and has no units.
F is the magnitude of the force, not its y-component.
The y-component is F sin 60° when the angle is measured from the x-axis.
F cos 60° gives the x-component of the force.
F tan 60° is not the y-component of a force with magnitude F.
With the lever arm and angle unchanged, increasing force does not decrease its moment.
Moment of force is proportional to force when the lever arm and angle are fixed.
The moment does not remain the same when the force increases.
The moment doubles only if the force itself doubles while the lever arm and angle stay fixed.

The atmosphere extends far beyond 100 km.
The atmosphere is commonly stated to extend to about 1,000 km.
10,000 km is much greater than the commonly stated height of the atmosphere.

Hooke’s law relates extension to applied force for an elastic object.
A hydraulic press works according to Pascal’s law: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted throughout it.
Conservation of energy is not the principle on which a hydraulic press operates.

Zero kelvin is absolute zero, not the melting point of ice.
32 is the melting point of ice in degrees Fahrenheit, not kelvin.
−273 is approximately the melting point of ice in degrees Celsius, not kelvin.
The melting point of ice is approximately 273 K.

Hitting a material does not magnetise it by the usual method and may weaken its magnetism.
Heating generally weakens or destroys magnetism rather than creating it.
An alternating-current solenoid is commonly used to demagnetise a material.
